newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Lufthansa group's Manila airport deal challenged.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa group's Manila airport deal challenged.

text.p: A Filipino company on Thursday said it filed a lawsuit to stop the award of a contract to a consortium, in which Lufthansa has a stake, to build a new terminal at Manila International airport.
Asia's Emerging Dragon Corp (AEDC), jointly owned by six Filipino-Chinese tycoons, said the civil complaint was filed at the Pasig City Regional Trial Court on April 16.

"AEDC has asked the Regional Trial Court to declare as null and void all the proceedings and acts of the Department of Transportation and Communications (DOTC) in connection with the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal III (NAIA-3) contract bidding," a statement issued by AEDC said.
The AEDC was invited by President Fidel Ramos to build the terminal under a build-operate-transfer (BOT) scheme.
But People's Aircargo & Warehousing Co Inc (PairCargo) submitted a better bid which AEDC declined to match. Lufthansa has a small stake in Paircargo.
The AEDC said the DOTC pre-qualified the PairCargo consortium despite its failure to raise the 30 percent minimum equity needed to finance the project.

"The consortium to date has not been able to raise the required equity for the project, nor provide proof of firm commitments from reputable financial institutions to provide sufficient credit lines to cover the total estimated cost of the project," the AEDC said.
The DOTC is yet to issue the notice of award after it extended the deadline twice for PairCargo to submit documents supporting its capability to put up the required equity.
DOTC and PairCargo officials were not immediately available to comment. - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418938 Fax 8176267
